content_sanskrit: दूराद्दूरमभिप्लुत्य शनैरुच्चैः पदं गते । हस्तं हस्ते समालम्ब्य यान्त्यौ ददृशतुर्नभः
padaccheda: दूरात् । दूरम् । अभिप्लुत्य । शनैः । उच्चैः । पदम् । गते । हस्तम् । हस्ते । समालम्ब्य । यान्त्यौ । ददृशतुः । नभः
anvaya: दूरात् दूरम् अभिप्लुत्य शनैः उच्चैः पदम् गते (ते उभे) हस्तम् हस्ते समालम्ब्य नभः यान्त्यौ ददृशतुः
meaning_english: Having leaped from distance to distance and gradually reached a high state, the two women, holding each other by the hand, beheld the sky as they traversed it.

padaccheda: एकार्णवम् । इव । उच्छूनम् । गम्भीरम् । निर्मलान्तरम् । कोमलम् । कोमलमरुदासङ्गसुखभोगदम्
anvaya: (तत् नभः) उच्छूनम् एकार्णवम् इव गम्भीरम् निर्मल-अन्तरम् कोमलम् कोमल-मरुत्-आसङ्ग-सुख-भोग-दम् (आसीत्)
meaning_english: The sky was like a swollen, singular ocean—deep, with a pure interior, soft, and bestowing the pleasure of contact with gentle breezes.

content_sanskrit: आह्लादकमलं सौम्यं शून्यताम्भोनिमज्जनात् । अत्यन्तशुद्धं गम्भीरं प्रसन्नमपि सज्जनात्
padaccheda: आह्लादकम् । अलम् । सौम्यम् । शून्यताम्भोनिमज्जनात् । अत्यन्तशुद्धम् । गम्भीरम् । प्रसन्नम् । अपि । सज्जनात्
anvaya: (तत् नभः) आह्लादकम् अलम् सौम्यम् शून्यता-अम्भः-निमज्जनात् अत्यन्त-शुद्धम् गम्भीरम् सत्-जनात् अपि प्रसन्नम् (आसीत्)
meaning_english: Delightful and exceedingly serene, it was extremely pure due to the immersion in the waters of emptiness, and deeper and more translucent even than the hearts of virtuous people.
They rested within the quarters of the sky, which were as pure as the interior of the full moon and served as a nectarous abode in the thick bellies of spotless clouds resting on mountain peaks.
They delighted in the sweet breezes that were charming with the fragrance of the mandāra garlands of Siddhas and Gandharvas, appearing as if they had issued from the lunar orb.

padaccheda: सस्नतुः । भूरिघर्मान्ते । तडिद्रक्ताब्जसंकुले । सरसि । इव । जलापूरमन्थरे । मेघमण्डले
anvaya: (ते) भूरि-घर्म-अन्ते तडिद्-रक्त-अब्ज-संकुले जला-पूर-मन्थरे मेघ-मण्डले सरसि इव सस्नतुः
meaning_english: At the end of their great heat, they bathed in the mass of clouds, which were crowded with lightning like red lotuses and sluggish with the fullness of water, as if in a lake.

content_sanskrit: भूतलौघमहाशैलमृणालाङ्कुरकोटिषु । दिक्षु बभ्रमतुः स्वैरं भ्रमर्यौ सरसीष्विव
padaccheda: भूतलौघमहाशैलमृणालाङ्कुरकोटिषु । दिक्षु । बभ्रमतुः । स्वैरम् । भ्रमर्यौ । सरसीषु । इव
anvaya: (ते) भूतल-ओघ-महा-शैल-मृणाल-अङ्कुर-कोटिषु दिक्षु सरसीषु भ्रमर्यौ इव स्वैरम् बभ्रमतुः
meaning_english: They wandered freely through the directions as bees do among lakes, treating the mass of the earth and the great mountains as if they were millions of lotus stalks and sprouts.
Thinking it to be a shower-house, they wandered through the pavilion of the cloud-mass agitated by the wind, which bore the steady torrents of the celestial Gaṅgā.

content_sanskrit: ततो मधुरगामिन्यौ विश्राम्यन्त्यौ स्वशक्तितः । शून्ये ददृशतुर्व्योम महारम्भातिमन्थरम्
padaccheda: ततः । मधुरगामिन्यौ । विश्राम्यन्त्यौ । स्वशक्तितः । शून्ये । ददृशतुः । व्योम । महारम्भातिमन्थरम्
anvaya: ततः मधुर-गामिन्यौ स्व-शक्तितः विश्राम्यन्त्यौ (ते) महा-आरम्भ-अति-मन्थरम् शून्ये व्योम ददृशतुः
meaning_english: Then, moving gracefully and resting according to their strength, they beheld the firmament in the void, appearing extremely sluggish despite its grand activities.

padaccheda: अदृष्टपूर्वम् । अन्योन्यम् । सर्वसंकटकोटरम् । अपूर्यमाणम् । आशून्यम् । जगत्कोटिशतैः । अपि
anvaya: (ते) अदृष्ट-पूर्वम् अन्योन्यम् सर्व-संकट-कोटरम् जगत्-कोटि-शतैः अपि अपूर्यमाणम् आ-शून्यम् (व्योम ददृशतुः)
meaning_english: They saw the void, never seen before, which is the hollow containing all calamities and remains unfilled and empty even by hundreds of millions of worlds.

padaccheda: उपरि । उपरि । उपरि । उच्चैः । अन्यैः । अन्यैः । वृतम् । पृथक् । विचित्राभरणाकारैः । भूतलैः । सुविमानकैः
anvaya: विचित्र-आभरण-आकारैः सु-विमानकैः (च) अन्यैः अन्यैः पृथक् भूतलैः उपरि उपरि उपरि उच्चैः वृतम् (इदं जगत् अस्ति)
meaning_english: The universe is surrounded higher and higher by various distinct terrestrial planes and beautiful celestial chariots, which are shaped like wonderful ornaments.

anvaya: परितः पूरित-व्योम्नाम् मेरु-आदि-कुल-भूभृताम् पद्मराग-तट-उद्द्योतैः कल्प-ज्वाला-उपम-उदरम् (इदं दृश्यते)
meaning_english: With the brilliance of ruby-colored slopes of the great mountain ranges like Meru filling the sky in all directions, the interior of the universe appears like the blazing fires of cosmic dissolution.
The cosmos looks as beautiful as the peaks of the Himavat due to the flood of light from pearl-like summits, and it shines like a golden land from the rays of the golden mountain's plateaus.

It possesses the greenness of grassy lands due to the luster of great emeralds, and it holds a blackness arising from the darkness produced when the observer and the observed merge at the end of perception.

anvaya: पारिजात-लता-लोल-विमान-गण-केतनम् अतः मञ्जरिका-आकारम् इव वैदूर्य-भूतलम् (इदं दृश्यते)
meaning_english: Decorated with the banners of celestial chariots swaying amidst Pārijāta vines, the lapis lazuli ground appears like a cluster of flower buds.

This space is filled with the coming and going of great Siddhas who move swifter than thought and conquer the winds, echoing with the jingling sounds of music and instruments played by celestial women in their aerial mansions.
The intervals of space are densely packed with the movements of the best beings of the three worlds, crowded with tribes of Suras and Asuras who move about without being seen by one another.
The edges of this space are inhabited by circles of Kūṣmāṇḍas, Rākṣasas, and Piśācas, while the multitude of celestial beings is carried along by the great velocity of the atmospheric winds.
The sky resounds with the whistling sounds of moving chariots and thick noises that seem tangible; its atmospheric mechanisms are set in motion by the dense movement of planets and stars.
This region contains abodes abandoned by lesser Siddhas scorched by the nearby sun-heat, and beautiful little chariots charred and tossed by the breath from the mouths of the Sun's horses.

The sky was flickering with the movements and activities of the Lokapālas and throngs of celestial nymphs; its atmosphere was filled with clouds formed from the smoke of incense burnt by the ladies in the queens' inner apartments.

The sky was strewn with ornaments fallen from the limbs of celestial women summoned from their respective heavens, and the darkness there was overpowered by the intense mass of radiance from the gathered Siddhas.
The mountains Himavat, Meru, and Mandara appeared as if draped in fine garments due to the clouds being tossed and scattered by the forceful coming and going of the milling crowds of Siddhas.

padaccheda: काकोलूकैः । गृध्रभासैः । राशिभूतैः । च । चलैः । वृतम् । नृत्यद्भिः । डाकिनीसङ्घैः । तरङ्गैः । इव । वारिधिम्
anvaya: (तद् आकाशम्) राशिभूतैः चलैः काक-उलूकैः गृध्र-भासैः (च) नृत्यद्भिः डाकिनी-सङ्घैः तरङ्गैरिव वारिधिम् (इव) वृतम् (अस्ति)।
meaning_english: Crowded with moving heaps of crows, owls, vultures, and Śakunta birds, and filled with dancing groups of Ḍākinīs, the sky resembled an ocean surging with waves.

padaccheda: प्रवृत्तैः । योगिनीसङ्घैः । श्व-काक-उष्ट्र-खर-आननैः । निरर्थम् । योजनशतम् । गत्वा । आगच्छद्भिः । आवृतम्
anvaya: (तद् आकाशम्) श्व-काक-उष्ट्र-खर-आननैः प्रवृत्तैः निरर्थं योजन-शतं गत्वा आगच्छद्भिः योगिनी-सङ्घैः आवृतम् (अस्ति)।
meaning_english: The sky was covered by bands of Yoginīs with the faces of dogs, crows, camels, and donkeys, who were aimlessly flying back and forth across hundreds of yojanas.
In the cloud-palaces, grey like the smoke and darkness of the cities of the Lokapālas, the sky witnessed the festivals of love commenced by couples of Siddhas and Gandharvas.

The pathways of the sky were occupied by those intoxicated by the songs and praises of heaven and smitten by Madana; it was marked by the continuous movement of the planetary spheres and celestial chariots.
The waters of the triple-pathed river (Gaṅgā) flowed within the foundations of the wind-zones; meanwhile, the children of the gods wandered about, eager to witness the wonders of the firmament.

anvaya: (तद् आकाशम्) स-देह-सञ्चरत्-वज्र-चक्र-शूल-असि-शक्ति-मत् क्वचित् निर्भित्ति भवनम् गायत्-नारद-तुम्बुरु (अस्ति)।
meaning_english: In some places, weapons like the Vajra, discus, trident, sword, and spear moved about in embodied forms; elsewhere, the sky served as a wall-less mansion where Nārada and Tumburu sang.

In some parts, the sky was agitated by the massive undertakings of great clouds in the celestial paths, while in others, the silent clouds of doomsday stood still, appearing like figures fixed in a painting.
The sky is sometimes filled with clouds as beautiful as rising mountains of black collyrium, and at other times with clouds glowing with the golden heat of the setting sun.
In some places, the sky wears clouds like a garment over the Ṛṣyamūka mountain, scorched by forest fires; elsewhere, it resembles a windless, surging ocean of pure emptiness.
Sometimes the sky carries celestial chariots like blades of grass in a river of wind, and sometimes it is as pure and dark as the glistening backs of a swarm of moving bees.
At times, it is grey with dust raised by winds like rivers flowing from Mount Meru; at others, it is variegated by the radiant light of deities in their celestial vehicles.
In some parts, it is encircled by the dancing circles of the naked Mātṛkā goddesses; in others, it is forever filled with groups of great female Yogīs, agitated as if newly intoxicated.
It is occasionally garlanded by sages resting in peaceful Samādhi, appearing as beautiful as the tranquil mind of a holy man whose worldly agitations have long been cast away.

padaccheda: गायत्-किन्नर-गन्धर्व-सुर-स्त्री-मण्डलम् । क्वचित् । क्वचित् । स्तब्ध-पुरा-कीर्णम् । वहत्-पुर-वरम् । क्वचित्
anvaya: (आकाशं) क्वचित् गायत्-किन्नर-गन्धर्व-सुर-स्त्री-मण्डलं (अस्ति), क्वचित् स्तब्ध-पुरा-कीर्णं, क्वचित् वहत्-पुर-वरम् (अस्ति) ।
meaning_english: In one place, there are choirs of singing Kinnaras, Gandharvas, and celestial nymphs; in another, it is crowded with ancient, motionless cities or great floating aerial cities.

padaccheda: क्वचित् । रुद्र-पुर-आपूर्णम् । क्वचित् । ब्रह्म-महा-पुरम् । क्वचित् । माया-कृत-पुरम् । क्वचित् । आगामि-पत्तनम्
anvaya: (आकाशं) क्वचित् रुद्र-पुर-आपूर्णं, क्वचित् ब्रह्म-महा-पुरं (अस्ति), क्वचित् माया-कृत-पुरं, क्वचित् आगामि-पत्तनम् (अस्ति) ।
meaning_english: The sky is sometimes filled with the cities of Rudra or the great city of Brahmā; at times, it contains illusory cities or the spectral outlines of cities yet to be built.

padaccheda: क्वचित् । भ्रमत्-चन्द्र-सरः । क्वचित् । स्तब्ध-मय-सरः । क्वचित् । सरत्-सिद्ध-गणम् । क्वचित् । इन्दु-कृत-उदयम्
anvaya: (आकाशं) क्वचित् भ्रमत्-चन्द्र-सरः, क्वचित् स्तब्ध-मय-सरः (अस्ति), क्वचित् सरत्-सिद्ध-गणं, क्वचित् इन्दु-कृत-उदयम् (अस्ति) ।
meaning_english: Sometimes it features the moon wandering like a lake, or the still lakes of the demon Maya; elsewhere, groups of Siddhas glide through it, or the moon begins its rise.

padaccheda: क्वचित् । सूर्य-उदय-मयम् । क्वचित् । रात्रि-तमः-मयम् । क्वचित् । संध्या-अंशुक-पिलम् । क्वचित् । नीहार-धूसरम्
anvaya: (आकाशं) क्वचित् सूर्य-उदय-मयं, क्वचित् रात्रि-तमः-मयं (अस्ति), क्वचित् संध्या-अंशुक-पिलं, क्वचित् नीहार-धूसरम् (अस्ति) ।
meaning_english: In some regions, the sky is filled with the rising sun, in others with the darkness of night; it is sometimes tawny like the robes of twilight and sometimes grey with frost and mist.

content_sanskrit: क्वचिद्धिमाभ्रधवलं क्वचिद्वर्षत्पयोधरम् । क्वचित्स्थल इवाकाश एव विश्रान्तलोकपम्
padaccheda: क्वचित् । हिमाभ्रधवलम् । क्वचित् । वर्षत्पयोधरम् । क्वचित् । स्थलः । इव । आकाशे । एव । विश्रान्तलोकपम्
anvaya: (आकाशम्) क्वचित् हिम-अभ्र-धवलम् क्वचित् वर्षत्-पयोधरम् क्वचित् स्थल इव (अस्ति) (तथा) आकाशे एव विश्रान्त-लोकपम् (अस्ति)
meaning_english: The sky is sometimes white like snowy clouds, sometimes heavy with raining clouds, and in some places it appears solid like land, serving as the resting place for the guardians of the world.

In some regions, the sky is crowded with throngs of gods and demons busy moving upward and downward, while in others it is bustling with movement across the eastern, western, northern, and southern directions.

content_sanskrit: अपि योजनलक्षाणि क्वचिद्दुष्प्रापभूधरम् । अविनाशितमःपूर्णं दृषद्गर्भोपमं क्वचित्
padaccheda: अपि । योजनलक्षाणि । क्वचित् । दुष्प्रापभूधरम् । अविनाशितमःपूर्णम् । दृषद्गर्भोपमम् । क्वचित्
anvaya: (आकाशम्) क्वचित् योजन-लक्षाणि अपि दुष्प्राप-भूधरम् (अस्ति) क्वचित् अविनाशि-तमः-पूर्णम् दृषत्-गर्भ-उपमम् (अस्ति)
meaning_english: The sky stretches for millions of yojanas where even mountains are hard to reach; elsewhere, it is filled with indestructible darkness, resembling the dense interior of a solid stone.

padaccheda: अविनाशिबृहत्तेजः । क्वचित् । अर्कानलोपमम् । हिमानीजठराशीतम् । क्वचित् । चन्द्रादिसद्मसु
anvaya: (आकाशम्) क्वचित् अर्क-अनल-उपमम् अविनाशि-बृहत्-तेजः (अस्ति) क्वचित् चन्द्र-आदि-सद्मसु हिमानी-जठर-आशीतम् (अस्ति)
meaning_english: In some parts, the sky radiates an eternal and great light comparable to the sun or fire, while in the abodes of the moon and others, it is as cold as the interior of a mass of snow.
In some places, it bears forests of wish-fulfilling trees and creepers stretching forward; in others, it contains the high cities of the gods falling down after being struck by demons.
The sky is sometimes marked with streaks of fire caused by the falling of celestial charioteers, and elsewhere it is scarred by the mutual collisions of hundreds of calamitous comets.

padaccheda: क्वचित् । शुभग्रहगणप्रगृहीताग्र्यमण्डलम् । क्वचित् । रात्रितमोव्याप्तम् । क्वचित् । दिवसभास्वरम्
anvaya: (आकाशम्) क्वचित् शुभ-ग्रह-गण-प्रगृहीत-अग्र्य-मण्डलम् (अस्ति) क्वचित् रात्रि-तमः-व्याप्तम् क्वचित् दिवस-भास्वरम् (अस्ति)
meaning_english: Sometimes its foremost regions are occupied by clusters of auspicious planets; at times it is pervaded by the darkness of night, and at others it is brilliant with the light of day.

padaccheda: क्वचित् । उद्गर्जदम्भोदम् । क्वचित् । मूकामलाम्बुदम् । वातावकीर्णशुक्लाभ्रखण्डपुष्पोत्तरम् । क्वचित्
anvaya: (आकाशम्) क्वचित् उद्गर्जत्-अम्भोदम् क्वचित् मूक-अमल-अम्बुदम् क्वचित् वात-अवकीर्ण-शुक्ल-अभ्र-खण्ड-पुष्प-उत्तरम् (अस्ति)
meaning_english: In certain areas, the sky contains thundering clouds, in others silent and pure clouds, and elsewhere it is strewn with fragments of white clouds scattered by the wind like flowers.

padaccheda: क्वचित् । अत्यन्तनिःशून्यम् । अवदातम् । अनन्तरम् । आनन्दमृदुशान्ताच्छम् । ज्ञस्य । इव । हृदयम् । ततम्
anvaya: (आकाशम्) क्वचित् अत्यन्त-निःशून्यम् अवदातम् अनन्तरम् ततम् ज्ञस्य हृदयम् इव आनन्द-मृदु-शान्त-अच्छम् (अस्ति)
meaning_english: In some parts, the sky is absolutely void, pure, infinite, and expansive—blissful, soft, peaceful, and clear like the heart of a wise man (jñānin).

padaccheda: शुक्रवाहनभेकौघैः । क्वचित् । गलकृतारवम् । शून्यतावारिवलितम् । क्षेत्रम् । आकाशवासिनाम्
anvaya: (आकाशम्) क्वचित् शुक्र-वाहन-भेक-ओघैः गल-कृत-आरवम् (अस्ति) (इदम्) शून्यता-वारि-वलितम् आकाश-वासिनाम् क्षेत्रम् (अस्ति)
meaning_english: In some places, it resounds with the croaking of frogs that serve as the vehicles of Śukra; this sky is a field for celestial dwellers, enveloped by the waters of emptiness.

padaccheda: मयूरहेमचूडादिपक्षिभिः । क्वचित् । आवृतम् । विद्याधरीणाम् । देवीनाम् । वाहनैः । विहितास्पदैः
anvaya: (तत् आकाशं) क्वचित् विहित-आस्पदैः विद्याधरीणाम् देवीनाम् वाहनैः मयूर-हेमचूड-आदि-पक्षिभिः आवृतम् (अस्ति) ।
meaning_english: In some places, the sky was covered by the avian vehicles of the goddesses of the Vidyādharas, such as peacocks and golden-crested birds, who had established their positions there.

padaccheda: क्वचित् । अभ्रान्तरोन्नृत्यद्गुहमायूरमण्डलम् । क्वचित् । अग्निशुकैः । श्यामम् । शाद्वलानाम् । इव । स्थलम्
anvaya: क्वचित् अभ्र-अन्तरे उन्नृत्यत्-गुह-मायूर-मण्डलम् (अस्ति), क्वचित् अग्निशुकैः शाद्वलानाम् स्थलम् इव श्यामम् (अस्ति) ।
meaning_english: In some parts, flocks of Guha’s peacocks danced within the clouds, while in others, the sky appeared dark green like a grassy meadow due to the presence of Agni-parrots.

padaccheda: क्वचित् । प्रेतेशमहिषमहिम्ना । वामनाम्बुदम् । क्वचित् । अश्वैः । तृणग्रामशङ्काग्रस्तासिताम्बुदम्
anvaya: क्वचित् प्रेतेश-महिष-महिम्ना वामन-अम्बुदम् (अस्ति), क्वचित् अश्वैः तृण-ग्राम-शङ्का-ग्रस्त-असित-अम्बुदम् (अस्ति) ।
meaning_english: In one area, the clouds appeared small compared to the greatness of Yama’s buffalo; in another, divine horses bit at dark clouds, mistaking them for bundles of grass.

padaccheda: क्वचित् । देवपुरव्याप्तम् । क्वचित् । दैत्यपुरान्वितम् । अन्योन्याप्राप्यनगरम् । नगरन्ध्रकरानिलम्
anvaya: (तत्) क्वचित् देव-पुर-व्याप्तम्, क्वचित् दैत्य-पुर-अन्वितम्, अन्योन्य-अप्राप्य-नगरम्, नगा-रन्ध्र-कर-अनिलम् (अस्ति) ।
meaning_english: The sky was filled with cities of gods in some places and cities of demons in others; these cities were inaccessible to one another, and the winds were strong enough to pierce through mountains.
In certain regions, it shone with the dancing form of Bhairava, who was as massive as a mountain range; in others, Vināyaka danced, appearing like a great winged mountain.
In some places, mountains were seen flying, lifted by the wings of gurgling gusts of wind; in others, it was beautiful with the cities of Gandharvas and celestial damsels.
In one part, clouds rose high, carrying hundreds of thousands of trees uprooted by moving mountains; in another, the air was cooled by the waters of illusory celestial lotuses.
In some areas, refreshing and pleasing breezes were drawn in by the moonbeams, while in others, trees, mountains, and clouds were scorched by hot winds.
In certain parts, it was utterly silent due to the complete stillness of the winds; in others, hundreds of mountain-like cloud peaks arose.
In some places, it echoed with the gurgling roar of intoxicated monsoon clouds; in others, it was impassable due to the battles raging between hosts of gods and demons.

In some places, the sky resounded with the calls of swans from the celestial lotus-pools, which seemed to invite Brahmā (the one seated on the lotus). In other places, a gentle breeze blew, having just finished plundering the fragrance of the lotuses on the banks of the celestial Mandākinī river.

Due to the proximity of the Gaṅgā and other celestial rivers, the sky itself appeared to hold within its body leaping fish, crocodiles, crabs, lotuses, and tortoises, looking as if they were flying through the firmament.
In various regions, the discs of the sun and moon appeared eclipsed by the shadow of the earth—likened to a dark crow—produced by the subterranean sun located in the netherworld (Pātāla).

Somewhere, the winds of creation shook the forest of the flowers of Māyā; elsewhere, the wives of the gods dwelling in celestial chariots were startled by the falling showers of flowers and cold frost.

padaccheda: उदुम्बरोदरमशकक्रमभ्रमज्जगत्त्रयान्तरगतभूतसंचयम् । विलङ्घ्य । तत् । वरललने । खम् । उच्चकैः । महीतलं । पुनः । अपि । गन्तुम् । उद्यते
anvaya: उदुम्बर-उदर-मशक-क्रम-भ्रमत्-जगत्-त्रय-अन्तर-गत-भूत-संचयम् (आकाशम्) विलङ्घ्य, तत्-वर-ललने! (ते) उच्चकैः खम् (त्यक्त्वा) पुनः अपि मही-तलम् गन्तुम् उद्यते (स्तः)।
meaning_english: O noble ladies! Having traversed the sky where multitudes of beings wander within the three worlds like gnats inside a ripening wild fig (Udumbara), those two are now preparing to leave the high heavens and descend once more to the surface of the earth.
